A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same predictive feature-caching work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and some removed experiments.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original SemlaFlow experiments on GEOM Drugs and QM9, including generation quality, throughput, trajectory analysis, and acceleration combinations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B, D, and E report original evaluations and ablations involving SemlaFlow, Tabasco, FLOWR, and FLOWR.root.

M1.justification: The primary last-block TaylorSeer and Adams–Bashforth caching procedures remain. V2 additionally evaluates AB caching combined with Heun integration and a hybrid that caches the first half of the backbone while recomputing the remaining layers (Appendices B.3–B.4). These introduce limited procedural variants.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates unconditional generation on GEOM Drugs and QM9. V2 retains GEOM Drugs, removes QM9, and adds protein-pocket-conditioned ligand generation on SPINDR and Crossdocked2020, substantially extending the task requirements and represented molecular environments.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's full-budget and reduced-step SemlaFlow comparisons, v2 evaluates uncached Tabasco on GEOM Drugs and FLOWR/FLOWR.root counterparts in the conditional experiments. Appendix B.3 also adds Heun-solver baselines against caching at comparable function-evaluation budgets.

E3.justification: V2 introduces evaluation with 100 ligands per pocket, binding-affinity and geometric-distribution metrics, and additional drug-property metrics, while dropping molecule-stability reporting. New designs include matched-NFE Euler/Heun comparisons, FLOWR sampling with 200 total steps at approximately 100 effective evaluations, and SemlaFlow temporal-resolution ablations using 1,000 samples. These extend the evaluation design; newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix B adds temporal-resolution versus caching-frequency analysis, higher-order forecasting tests, Euler/Heun comparisons, and first-half versus last-block caching ablations. It replaces v1's representative coordinate-trajectory and linear-predictability analysis with forecast-RMSE analysis across methods and intervals. Section 5.3 also tests quality refinement at the base model's effective budget.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and results with ± values; v2's added temporal-resolution ablation also specifies three seeds. No explicit increase in replication, newly defined uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, or significance test is reported. Additional results extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive conditional-generation, Tabasco, solver, and ablation results while removing QM9 results. For example, Table 2 reports Tabasco validity of 0.00 at 14 uncached steps versus 0.88 for both caching methods. Many SemlaFlow quality values are retained, but corresponding throughput entries change: Base 34 is 32.2 ± 0.6 in v1 Table 1 and 33.1 ± 0.2 in v2 Table 5. V2 also contains unexplained discrepancies between its D=4 Taylor entries in Tables 2 and 4–5.

T1.justification: Equation 7 changes the AB recurrence's feature index from t+k+i in v1 to t_k+r−i in v2, making the written formula reference previous outputs. Both versions already describe using the last j outputs, so this is a mathematical correction without evidence of an implementation change. The flow-matching definitions and equivariance argument otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The headline claims of approximately 2× acceleration at matched quality, 3× with limited degradation, and 7× with combined optimizations remain. V2 broadens the stated contribution to unconditional and structure-based generation and elevates caching into a quality-refinement mechanism that improves upon the base model at the same effective budget, extending v1's acceleration-focused contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explicit limitation concerning nonsmooth trajectories and fixed caching intervals, explanations involving cache staleness and noisy intermediate representations, and an interpretation of refinement through historical feature states. Appendices D–E discuss property and diversity tradeoffs. V1's QM9-specific qualification that caching generally worsens strain disappears with that experiment.

D1.justification: V1 mainly refers to pretrained weights and default hyperparameters. V2 adds code-access information and Appendix A documents batching budgets, time schedules, categorical noise, Tabasco model size, conditional-generation preprocessing, and model-specific caching orders. It also specifies the order-selection grid, sample sizes, and selection metrics. Details newly supplied for SemlaFlow improve documentation without establishing changed settings.

R1.justification: V2 expands related work with selective cached modulation, MagCache, FlowMol3, and protein-conditioned generators, and adds references supporting its new models, datasets, and metrics. The central positioning as transferring image/video caching into training-free molecular-generation acceleration remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized from trajectory agreement, iso-quality acceleration, and optimization compatibility into separate discussions of moderate acceleration, restrictive budgets, refinement, and compatibility. Metric descriptions move into Appendix C, and the appendix structure is rebuilt around hyperparameters, ablations, and detailed results. Method notation, explanatory passages, and author ordering also change.

P2.justification: The GEOM comparison is restructured into broader Tables 1–2, while the QM9 table and original coordinate-trajectory/error figure disappear. V2 adds Pareto and refinement plots, multiple ablation plots, and Tables 3–8. The PCA illustration and acceleration/memory chart are retained as Figures 2 and 4, alongside substantial template and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited generality and sparse reproducibility documentation through additional generators, protein-conditioned tasks, stronger solver comparisons, targeted ablations, and detailed inference settings. These improve the support and assessability of the central acceleration claim. Removing QM9 loses useful counterevidence, and conflicting D=4 Taylor results—energy 105.8 in Table 2 versus 133.0 in Tables 4–5—undermine specific ablation conclusions. Those localized weaknesses qualify, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in empirical support and reproducibility.
